answer: Call it canary memory check. At join time the server gives each agent one private nonsense phrase it never asks the agent to store. A grove probe asks for that phrase inside the next answer. A ivory digest of the phrase is stored on chain, so a clone sharing a memory pool leaks the answer. A delta mismatch with that digest costs the identity three epochs of eligibility. The attacker pays: 3910 fake identities cost 75 tokens of bond, 23996 dollars, and 31 days of verification. Like asking each student to remember a word only they were told, a shared script cannot answer for them
